clips.text: Everything so far has lived in the present: order this, ask that, right now. Today the trip gets a past tense — three verbs that let you tell someone what yesterday actually was.
¿Qué hiciste ayer?
Fui — I went. The whole day starts with where you went, and that one word carries the whole sentence.
Say where you went yesterday. Speak now.
Fui al mercado.
¿Y qué comiste?
Comí — I ate. Same pattern, different verb. The story is building itself one short sentence at a time.
Say what you ate. Speak now.
Comí tacos al pastor.
And the verb that closes the story with feeling, not just fact: me encantó. It loved-me, literally — the thing did the loving, in Spanish grammar. But it lands exactly like 'I loved it.'
Say you loved it. Speak now.
Me encantó.
¿Y hoy qué van a hacer?
The conversation naturally swings forward too. You don't need a new tense for tomorrow — vamos a plus what you'll do covers it.
Say what you're going to do today. Speak now.
Vamos a ir a la playa.
Fui al mercado. Comí tacos al pastor. Me encantó.

I06 complete. Fui, comí, me encantó — three verbs, and yesterday becomes a real story instead of a list of nouns. Vamos a covers tomorrow. You now have a past and a future, not just an endless present.
Someone asks about yesterday. Listen for the three verbs that carry the whole story.
¿Qué hiciste ayer?
Fui al mercado. Comí tacos al pastor. Me encantó.
¿Y hoy qué van a hacer?
Vamos a ir a la playa.
